examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral
examples.problem:
The area of $ABCD$ is $300\, \text{cm}^2.$  What is the area of $\triangle ABC$ rounded to the nearest integer?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/c06ffb123bdd24c3f83419767b6d1578223b8093089b79f91aae8f1fc6121305.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ACD.$ We get 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot DA\cdot DC\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡D \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(25)(32)\operatorname{sin}⁡{70}^{∘} \\  & =400\operatorname{sin}⁡{70}^{∘} \\  & =375.877... \\  & ≈376\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ and $\triangle ACD$ gives the area of $\triangle ABC.$ Therefore, 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABC} & ={A}_{ACD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =376-300 \\  & =76\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACD$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/a60b049aef53aef28802b084b3e445fd6253978500ca981d3b799977523cdd71.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACD,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACD} & =\frac{1}{2}(8)(5)\operatorname{sin}⁡{55}^{∘} \\  & =20\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{55}^{∘} \\  & ≈16.383,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACD} \\  & =2\cdot 16.383 \\  & =32.766.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $33.$
